newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals sees much more stable S.African rand in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Stals sees much more stable S.African rand in 1997.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Tuesday he believed the rand would hold relatively stable in 1997 after its sharp depreciation last year.

In an interview, Stals said the rise in the currency this year meant that the rand had fallen by a net 16 percent against a basket of currencies in the last 14 months. He said this was roughly equivalent to two years' worth of inflation differentials between South Africa and its major trading partners.
"If we've had 16 percent over the last 14 months we have used up the 'quota' for 1997 and 1996," he said.

"I think the exchange rate has adjusted itself through market forces back to fundamentals, to the inflation differentials. And it is for that reason that we believe that in 1997 we will see a much more stable foreign exchange market."
